description: From defk-7a6 (merged). In a case guard such as rem(n, y) < n * n with y = 0 and n * n overflowing i64, native raises ArithmeticError (overflow is a limit) while Elixir mode's try/rescue sees the zero divisor first and makes the guard false, so the two modes disagree. Documented in docs/language.md as a known edge; not covered by an agreement test (only the overflow-first order is). Fix: Elixir mode should apply the limit check for every operand of the guard before deciding false (e.g. evaluate with limit-checked ops that collect both flags, raise if any limit flag is set, as native's govf replay does), or native should treat a guard containing a real guard error as false regardless of overflow order if that matches Elixir. Done when an agreement test with y = 0 and an overflowing n * n passes in both orders.

comments.text:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Agent Brief

**Category:** bug
**Summary:** A case guard that hits a real guard error fails the clause even when it also overflows i64, in native and Elixir mode, as Elixir does

**Decision (maintainer, triage 2026-10-11):** option A: native follows Elixir. A guard with a real guard error (zero divisor in div/rem//, inf/NaN float result) anywhere in what it evaluates is false, regardless of an i64 overflow in the same guard; the overflow limit (ArithmeticError) applies only when the guard has no real guard error.

**Current behavior (reproduced in triage, n = 4_000_000_000, y = 0):**

| guard | native | Elixir mode |
|---|---|---|
| `rem(m, y) < m * m` | ArithmeticError | false (returns the next clause) |
| `m * m > rem(m, y)` | ArithmeticError | ArithmeticError |

Plain Elixir (no overflow) fails the guard in both orders. docs/language.md (case guards "Limit" paragraph and the Limits table row for i64 overflow inside a case guard) documents the disagreement.

**Desired behavior:**
- Both orders: native and Elixir mode fail the guard (next clause / CaseClauseError), matching Elixir.
- A guard whose only problem is overflow still raises ArithmeticError in both modes (unchanged limit).
- Short-circuit semantics are unchanged: an operand an `and`/`or`/`andalso`/`orelse` skips never runs and contributes no error or overflow.
- Non-guard code is unchanged; guards with no fallible operation compile as before (no added cost).

**Key interfaces:**
- Guard lowering in the compiler (the guard error flag and the overflow flag, `govf`) and the Elixir-mode guard evaluation (`Defk.ElixirMode` / `Defk.ElixirMode.Ops`)
- docs/language.md: remove the "both a zero divisor and such a result" caveat and adjust the Limits row

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] Agreement tests (Defk.Test.assert_agrees) with y = 0 and an overflowing n * n pass in both operand orders, and both return the fallback clause
- [ ] Overflow-only guards still raise ArithmeticError in both modes (existing tests keep passing)
- [ ] A short-circuit case: an error or overflow in a skipped operand has no effect
- [ ] Forced-yield run of the new tests (`__defk_force_yields__/1`) where the guard sits in a loop
- [ ] `mix test`, `mix docs`, `mix credo --strict` clean

**Out of scope:**
- Changing which operations count as guard errors
- Overflow semantics outside guards

Merged with one rule beyond the triage decision: an overflowed i64 that would itself DECIDE the guard (left side of and/or outside the top-level-and exception, or feeding a divisor/float operand) raises ArithmeticError in both modes, because native cannot know the bignum value Elixir would have had — the alternatives were silent wrong answers or bignum guard evaluation in C. Both modes agree (the oracle invariant holds); documented in docs/language.md (guard Limit paragraph + Limits row), pinned by ovf_decides_or / ovf_not_and / ovf_divisor. Flag if you want this reopened.

title: Elixir mode returns false where native raises: a guard with both a zero divisor and an i64 overflow
